head: WhatsApp backup on iPhone without iCloud: beta tests its own servers
dek: Some WhatsApp beta testers on iPhone (version 26.45.10.71) can now back up their chats to WhatsApp's own end-to-end encrypted servers instead of iCloud. WhatsApp hasn't said when everyone gets it, and iCloud stays the default.
details: The WhatsApp option includes 2 GB free; WhatsApp Plus at $2.49 a month gives 100 GB, and Meta One plans up to 4 TB, according to MacRumors. It covers chat backups only. Code for the choice of backup place first showed up in beta builds in July, and Android already has this option. On 22 November WABetaInfo reported the same choice rolling out to Android beta testers (version 2.26.46.4) as an alternative to Google Drive; backups on WhatsApp's servers can't be restored on the other platform, and the latest one is kept for 4 months after a paid plan ends.
where: Some iPhone beta testers on TestFlight now; no date for everyone
means: If your iCloud storage is full and WhatsApp backups keep failing, a free 2 GB backup on WhatsApp's servers may help once it comes out for everyone.
todo: Nothing to do yet unless you're in the TestFlight beta, where the choice sits in the chat backup settings. Until then, keep your iCloud backup on.
